clue.text: Artist in state at flipping opera

indicators.note: the artist sits inside the name of the state, so one piece is cut open by the other

parts.note: Latvia is a Baltic state
RA, a Royal Academician, is the crossword's usual artist

indicators.note: flipping turns the little word at over, so it reads backwards

explanation.surface: A painter in some state, pictured somersaulting at the opera.
explanation.walkthrough: Latvia is the Baltic state; RA (Royal Academician) is the usual artist. 'flipping' reverses the clue's 'at'.
explanation.definitionFit: Verdi's famous work about Violetta is an example of an opera.

clue.text: Instrument female dropped for another one

indicators.note: the female letter is let fall from the instrument, so it is removed

parts.note: the flute is a woodwind instrument

explanation.surface: A woman leaves one instrument for a different one in the band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Instrument' looks like the definition, but it is the flute; 'another one' defines, meaning another instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A plucked stringed instrument of the Renaissance, so a further example of an instrument.

clue.text: After time, request church working party

indicators.note: the request comes after the time, placing the time letter first in the charade

parts.note: to request something is to ask for it
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A churchgoer, after a while, asks for a working party to be formed.
explanation.definitionFit: A group formed to do a particular job is a synonym for a working party.

clue.text: Scene of conflict in region housing indefinite number

indicators.note: the region houses the number, holding it inside itself

parts.note: a region is an area
N stands for an unspecified number in maths

explanation.surface: A battle zone in a region that shelters an unknown number of people.
explanation.definitionFit: A place where contests or fights happen, a synonym for a scene of conflict.

clue.text: From Spain, fantastic royal daughter

indicators.note: the letters are taken from within the words that follow, so they lie concealed there

explanation.surface: A wonderful princess from Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'From Spain' as part of the description; it is the pointer to letters inside 'Spain, fantastic'.
explanation.definitionFit: Spanish and Portuguese title for a king's daughter who is not heir, a royal princess.

clue.text: A kind of racing article having little depth?

parts.note: the definite article
something flat has little depth

explanation.surface: A shallow piece of writing about some sort of horse racing.
explanation.walkthrough: Flat racing is British horse racing without jumps.
explanation.definitionFit: Horse racing over courses without fences, a particular kind of racing season in Britain.

clue.text: Fish, black as soot initially

parts.note: B is the pencil abbreviation for black

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of soot

explanation.surface: A fish as black as soot.
explanation.definitionFit: A common sea and freshwater fish, an example of a fish.

clue.text: At Hogwarts, Dumbledore was one up

parts.note: A means one
Dumbledore was the headmaster, the head, of Hogwarts school in Harry Potter

explanation.surface: A fact about Harry Potter's headmaster at his wizarding school.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in front in a game or contest, as in one goal up, a synonym.

clue.text: Schedule this month, one no longer changeable

parts.note: to schedule a date is to set it
INST, instant, is old commercial shorthand for this month

explanation.surface: Booking something this month that cannot then be moved.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for something fixed and unalterable, like words carved into rock.

clue.text: Having head of security inside gallery makes sense

indicators.note: the leading letter sits inside the gallery's name

parts.note: the Tate is a London art gallery

indicators.note: head of picks the first letter of security

explanation.surface: Putting a security chief in the gallery is sensible.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the five senses, the one using the tongue.

clue.text: One under no compulsion to release spy

parts.note: to release is to free
a spy is a secret agent

explanation.surface: Someone who need not let a captured spy go.
explanation.definitionFit: A person able to act independently, bound by no contract or obligation.

clue.text: Do without it, as ban involved

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so these letters are mixed together

explanation.surface: Go without it, since a prohibition is in force.
explanation.definitionFit: To refrain from something, such as alcohol, is to go without it.

clue.text: Blandishments, fine lines describing former queen

parts.note: F is the pencil abbreviation for fine

indicators.note: describing in the sense of drawing round, the outer letters surround the queen

parts.note: L is line, LL lines
Queen Anne reigned over Britain until 1714

explanation.surface: Flattery from elegant verses written about an old queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'describing' means drawing a line around: FLL goes round ANNE.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang, smooth flattering talk or evasive patter is a synonym for blandishments.

clue.text: Danse macabre in saloon

indicators.note: macabre suggests something grotesquely distorted, telling us to reorder the letters

explanation.surface: Saint-Saens's Danse Macabre playing in a bar.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface borrows the title of Saint-Saens's piece; 'saloon' is a car, not a bar.
explanation.definitionFit: A saloon is the British word for the closed four-door car Americans call by this name.

clue.text: Destroy old book, well-read

parts.note: someone well-read is literate

explanation.surface: Wreck an ancient volume, educated though you are.
explanation.definitionFit: To wipe out completely is a synonym for destroy.

clue.text: Teacher in a flap, recalled coffee shop worker

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the assembled letters run in reverse
the teacher goes inside the flap

parts.note: a tab is a small flap
SIR is the schoolchild's name for a male teacher

explanation.surface: A teacher in a panic remembers the person who made her coffee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' reverses ATSIRAB, the teacher inside A TAB.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who makes and serves espresso drinks in a café, a coffee shop worker.

clue.text: It's to be raised, bishop winning support for a jockey

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means lifted up the column, so read backwards

parts.note: taken as the letters I T S
RR, Right Reverend, is a bishop's title
a side that is up is winning

explanation.surface: A bishop backs a jockey who is ahead in a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be raised' turns ITS into STI.
explanation.definitionFit: The metal loop hanging from the saddle supports a rider's foot.

clue.text: Send male out to get carriage

indicators.note: the male letter is put out of the word for send

parts.note: to send a signal is to transmit it

explanation.surface: Dispatch a man to fetch a horse-drawn coach.
explanation.definitionFit: Conveyance of goods or people from place to place, a sense of carriage.

clue.text: Maybe four, score for stroke made by batsman?

parts.note: four is a square number, two times two
to score a line is to cut it

explanation.surface: A batsman's shot that could go for four runs.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a four is a boundary, so 'Maybe four' poses as runs; it is a square number. A square cut is a cricket shot.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket shot hitting the ball square of the wicket on the off side, a batting stroke.

clue.text: List that is full of incorrect times

indicators.note: the abbreviation holds the other letters within it

parts.note: IE, id est, means that is

indicators.note: incorrect says the letters are set wrongly, so rearrange them

explanation.surface: A timetable riddled with wrong times.
explanation.walkthrough: IE is Latin id est, 'that is'; 'incorrect' scrambles the clue's 'times' before it goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To set out item by item is a synonym for list as a verb.

clue.text: Young Miss Havisham set off with Miss Fitzgerald

indicators.note: off means not right, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: Ella Fitzgerald, the jazz singer

explanation.surface: A young lady from Dickens departs with a jazz singer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' turns SET into EST. Estella is the girl Miss Havisham raises in Great Expectations.
explanation.definitionFit: The adopted ward of the jilted bride in Dickens's novel, a younger Havisham.

clue.text: Writer with firearm bagging one bird

parts.note: a pen is something to write with

indicators.note: the firearm bags, so holds inside, the single letter

parts.note: a gun is a firearm
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An author with a rifle shoots a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A flightless Antarctic seabird, an example of a bird.

clue.text: Trained and incisive

definitions.meaning: aimed, as a gun is directed at a target
sharp and cutting, as a remark can be

explanation.surface: Someone well-schooled and sharp.
explanation.definitionFit: Directed at something, and also sharp or barbed, as of a comment.

clue.text: Log that may be turned into treen

indicators.note: the letters of treen can be turned round into another word

explanation.surface: A wooden log that a woodturner might make into small wooden objects.
explanation.walkthrough: Treen is small wooden ware made on a lathe, which fits the woodworking picture.
explanation.definitionFit: To log data is to record it, a synonym in its verb sense.

clue.text: Coach tour rearranged to take in Turkey's capital

indicators.note: the jumbled letters take in, so contain, the single letter
rearranged tells us to reorder the letters of tour
capital means the opening, capital letter of Turkey

explanation.surface: A bus tour reorganised to include Ankara.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rearranged' gives TUOR, which takes in T.
explanation.definitionFit: A private teacher who coaches a pupil, a synonym for coach.

clue.text: Person going to Margate perhaps runs into truck

indicators.note: the runs abbreviation goes into the truck

parts.note: a tipper is a truck that tips its load
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A traveller to the seaside drives into a lorry.
explanation.walkthrough: Margate is an English seaside resort popular with day visitors.
explanation.definitionFit: A day visitor on an excursion, a holidaymaker heading for a resort.

clue.text: Flat's electric current shown in diagram

indicators.note: the current is shown inside the diagram, so it sits within it

parts.note: a plan is a diagram
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: An apartment's wiring marked on a drawing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flat' looks like an apartment; it is the adjective meaning level.
explanation.definitionFit: Level, unbroken ground, as in a broad plain, is a synonym of flat.

clue.text: Shock caused by dangerous feat? No end

indicators.note: no end means the final letter of the feat word is lost

parts.note: a stunt is a daring feat

explanation.surface: A daredevil's never-ending feat causing alarm.
explanation.definitionFit: To stun is to astonish or shock.

clue.text: High-flier's stand-in car I parked in allotment

parts.note: auto is short for automobile, a car

indicators.note: I is parked inside the allotment

parts.note: a plot is an allotment of land

explanation.surface: A stand-in at the allotment where I left the car.
explanation.walkthrough: An allotment is a rented British garden plot. 'High-flier' is a pilot, literally.
explanation.definitionFit: The automatic system that flies an aircraft takes the place of a human pilot.

clue.text: A British national racecourse

parts.note: a Scot is a native of Scotland, a part of Britain

explanation.surface: A British national racecourse.
explanation.walkthrough: Ascot is an English racecourse famous for Royal Ascot.
explanation.definitionFit: The Berkshire track famous for its royal meeting is an example of a racecourse.

clue.text: Take home unopened tea service

indicators.note: unopened means the first letter of tea is removed

parts.note: RN, the Royal Navy, is one of the armed services

explanation.surface: Bringing home an unused tea set.
explanation.definitionFit: Take-home pay is what you earn, so take home is a synonym for be paid.

clue.text: Stuffing not put back in bear

parts.note: padding is stuffing

indicators.note: put back means the word not is set in reverse

explanation.surface: Stuffing left out of a teddy bear.
explanation.definitionFit: Michael Bond's marmalade-loving bear from Peru, an example of a bear in fiction.
